reasoning: The extract sets out a clear evaluation plan. It cites a statutory duty to carry out a Post Implementation Review before 30 April 2017, and a later review date of 01/2021 tied to the European Commission's Package Travel Directive review due by 1 January 2021. Line 79 gives the purpose: to understand how the policy was implemented, whether objectives were met, and whether there were unintended consequences. It says the review will be 'light-touch' because of ATOL reform and expected Package Travel Regulations changes, and that results 'will help to inform the future direction of the ATOL programme'. Line 81 (Reference: 9) says the earlier Impact Assessment's cost and benefit estimates will be checked and better estimates used in future appraisal. Consultation is planned: six specific questions on certainty, competitiveness, time costs, bond costs, IT costs and unintended consequences, with businesses invited to respond. This is more than level 1, because it covers measures, evaluation and consultation, and it reaches level 2. The strongest counter-example to level 3 is that the document never says whether or when the results will be published, and gives no testing plan or reason for omitting one. The 'light-touch' choice is justified only briefly. To reach level 3, it would need to commit to publishing the PIR findings with a date, explain why this evaluation design was chosen, and state how the results will feed into decisions.
